items.followUp: Name three factors that affect the solubility of a substance.

rubric.why: One mark for naming a valid factor that affects solubility.
rubric.description: Names one factor affecting solubility.
rubric.how: Accept temperature, pressure, or the nature of the solute and solvent.

rubric.why: A second distinct factor is needed for full credit.
rubric.description: Names a second distinct factor affecting solubility.
rubric.how: Award for any second valid factor.

modelAnswer: The factors affecting solubility include the nature of the solute and solvent, temperature, and pressure (especially for gases).

items.followUp: Name any four metals that are highly reactive.

rubric.why: One mark is awarded for correctly naming two least reactive metals.
rubric.description: Names any two least reactive metals.
rubric.how: Accept any two distinct metals from the listed least reactive metals.

rubric.why: The question asks for four metals; this mark covers the other two.
rubric.description: Names two more least reactive metals.
rubric.how: Accept any two additional distinct metals from gold, silver, platinum, and copper.

modelAnswer: Gold, silver, platinum, and copper are among the least reactive metals.

items.followUp: State how atomic size changes down a group in the periodic table.

rubric.why: The required trend is an increase in electropositivity from top to bottom of a group.
rubric.description: States that electropositivity increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award full credit for both the direction and the trend.

modelAnswer: Electropositivity increases down a group in the periodic table.

items.followUp: Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of chlorine with hydrogen and name the product.

rubric.why: Fluorine reacts very vigorously with hydrogen.
rubric.description: Describes the reaction as vigorous or explosive.
rubric.how: Accept a clear statement that the reaction is very rapid or vigorous.

rubric.why: The reaction forms hydrogen fluoride, HF.
rubric.description: Gives the product or balanced equation.
rubric.how: Accept the product HF / hydrogen fluoride or the balanced equation H₂ + F₂ → 2HF.

modelAnswer: Fluorine reacts very vigorously with hydrogen to form hydrogen fluoride.
H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2HF(g)

items.followUp: State any four conclusions drawn from Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed through undeflected.
rubric.how: Accept wording that most particles passed straight through or were not deflected.

rubric.why: A small number of alpha particles were deflected from their paths.
rubric.description: States that a few alpha particles were deflected.
rubric.how: Accept a statement that some or a few particles changed direction.

rubric.why: Only a very small number of particles were scattered backwards.
rubric.description: States that very few alpha particles bounced back.
rubric.how: Accept rebounded, returned, or bounced back.

rubric.why: The large fraction passing through showed that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.description: Concludes that the atom is mostly empty space.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent wording.

rubric.why: The backward scattering showed that the atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus containing most of its mass.
rubric.description: Describes the nucleus as small, dense, and positively charged, or as containing most atomic mass.
rubric.how: Accept the key nucleus characteristics or the conclusion that most mass is concentrated in the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without deflection.
A few alpha particles were deflected through small angles.
Very few alpha particles were deflected through large angles or bounced back.
Most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
The atom has a very small, dense, positively charged nucleus that contains most of its mass.

items.followUp: Write any four properties of a mixture.

rubric.why: A compound has a definite composition and fixed proportions of its elements.
rubric.description: States that compounds have a fixed composition.
rubric.how: Accept definite or fixed composition/proportions.

rubric.why: A compound's properties differ from those of its constituent elements.
rubric.description: States that a compound has properties different from its constituent elements.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent wording about the compound's properties differing from those of its elements.

rubric.why: Elements in a compound are chemically combined.
rubric.description: States that elements are chemically combined in a compound.
rubric.how: Accept chemically combined or chemical combination.

rubric.why: A compound can be separated into its elements only by chemical methods.
rubric.description: States that compounds can be decomposed only by chemical means.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent wording indicating chemical, not physical, separation.

modelAnswer: A compound has a fixed composition, with its elements present in definite proportions.
Its properties are different from the properties of its constituent elements.
Its elements are chemically combined.
It can be decomposed into its elements only by chemical methods.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and describe any three factors that affect its rate.

rubric.why: Evaporation is vaporization from the surface of a liquid and can occur below its boiling point.
rubric.description: Defines evaporation as the change of a liquid into vapour at its surface.
rubric.how: Accept a definition mentioning surface vaporization; include below boiling point if stated.

rubric.why: Higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature.
rubric.how: Accept that increasing temperature increases evaporation.

rubric.why: A larger exposed surface area increases evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of surface area.
rubric.how: Accept that increasing surface area increases evaporation.

rubric.why: Moving air carries away vapour and increases evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of wind or air movement.
rubric.how: Accept that greater wind/air movement increases evaporation or removes vapour.

rubric.why: Higher humidity reduces the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of humidity.
rubric.how: Accept that evaporation is slower at higher humidity and faster at lower humidity.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface, and it can occur below the boiling point.
Increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
Increasing the exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
Greater wind or air movement carries vapour away and increases evaporation.
Higher humidity decreases the rate of evaporation; lower humidity increases it.

items.followUp: Define an unsaturated solution and explain how a supersaturated solution can be prepared.

rubric.why: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve at a specified temperature.
rubric.description: Defines a saturated solution at a given temperature.
rubric.how: Accept wording that no more solute can dissolve or that the maximum amount is dissolved.

rubric.why: An appropriate example illustrates the saturated solution.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a saturated solution.
rubric.how: Accept a saturated sugar-water or salt-water solution, or another valid example.

rubric.why: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution at the same temperature.
rubric.description: Defines a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: The comparison must be with the saturation limit at the same temperature.

rubric.why: A supersaturated solution may be prepared by carefully cooling a hot saturated solution; it is unstable and excess solute can crystallize.
rubric.description: Gives a valid preparation method or example/behaviour of a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: Accept careful cooling of a hot saturated solution or an example such as supersaturated sugar solution that forms crystals.

modelAnswer: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a particular temperature.
For example, a sugar solution is saturated when no more sugar dissolves at that temperature.
A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than a saturated solution can normally contain at the same temperature.
It can be prepared by dissolving extra solute in a hot saturated solution and then cooling it carefully; it is unstable and excess solute may crystallize out.
